title: Fix Deep Stack Overflow (Trampoline / Iterative Traversal)
concept: Tail-Call Trampolining & Heap vs Stack Allocation
problemStatement: A standard recursive traversal of a deep linked list crashes with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` for large N. Implement `safeTraverse(head)` that iterates through the list without exhausting the call stack, returning the total count of nodes.
interviewTrap: Candidates often write simple recursion `count(node.next) + 1` which overflows around 10,000 calls in V8. Converting to an iterative loop or trampoline moves frames from call stack to heap memory.

testCases.name: Counts 3-node linked list
testCases.testFn: const list = { val: 1, next: { val: 2, next: { val: 3, next: null } } }; return safeTraverse(list);

testCases.name: Traverses 30,000 nodes without stack overflow
testCases.testFn: let head = null; for(let i = 0; i < 30000; i++) { head = { val: i, next: head }; } return safeTraverse(head);

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Standard recursion accumulates stack frames linearly, causing a stack overflow (RangeError) for deep trees or large collections. The Trampoline pattern and iterative stack traversal transform recursive algorithm control flows into an iterative loop, trading call stack frames for heap-allocated thunk closures or arrays.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Replace synchronous deep recursive tree traversal with an explicit heap-allocated stack: `const stack = [root]`.
Loop synchronously while the heap stack is non-empty (`while (stack.length > 0)`).
Pop the current node from the stack, accumulate its value into the sum accumulator.
Push its right and left children onto the stack to preserve traversal order.
Return the accumulated sum once the queue is exhausted, consuming O(1) call stack frames.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: Engines allocate memory for call frames on the thread's fixed-size execution stack (typically 1MB). In contrast, the JavaScript memory heap can grow dynamically to gigabytes (bounded by `--max-old-space-size`). Iterative traversal completely bypasses stack overflow limitations by keeping data on the heap.

complexity.time: O(N) where N is the total number of nodes in the binary tree.
complexity.space: O(D) heap space where D is the maximum depth of the tree (O(1) Call Stack space).

edgeCasesHandled: Empty tree (root === null or undefined) returns 0 safely.
Extremely deep linear trees (e.g., 20,000 degenerate left-child nodes) process smoothly without stack overflow.
Standard multi-branch binary trees calculate exact sums.

specifications: ECMA-262 §15.10 Tail Call Optimization (Note: TCO is only supported in strict mode JavaScriptCore; V8 dropped syntactic TCO, necessitating trampolining/iteration)
V8 Blog: Tail Call Optimization analysis and heap-based trampolining
verifiedRules: Heap-based iteration eliminates recursive activation record allocation on the V8 C++ stack.
Iterative traversal is the standard production design pattern for AST walkers in Babel and TypeScript compiler.
